newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Major non-bank creditors agree to help Kia Group.
newsitem.headline: Major non-bank creditors agree to help Kia Group.

text.p: Daehan Investment Banking Corp and seven other South Korean merchant banks on Friday agreed to cooperate with the Kia Group in its efforts to normalise management, they said in a joint statement.
An official at the Merchant Banks Association of Korea, which comprises the eight firms and 22 other merchant banks, said the eight firms were major lenders to the Kia Group.
The statement did not name all the eight firms, but the association official said they included Shinhan Investment Bank, First Merchant Bank and Tongyang Merchant Bank.
Merchant banks have widely been criticised for worsening the financial troubles of companies struggling under heavy debts by hastily calling in commercial notes.
The statement said merchant banking firms would only call in notes on behalf of other financial institutions.
One of the Kia Group's main creditors, the Korea First Bank, announced on Tuesday it would bail out the group's flagship Kia Motors Corp and 17 other units.

The nation's eighth-largest Kia Group had 9.54 trillion won in debts owed to financial institutions as of the end of May, of which 4.36 trillion won was owed to merchant banking and insurance firms, according to the Korean Federation of Banks.
